title: Keep only the string items
description: Write a function `get_string_lists(items)` that returns a new list containing only the items of `items` that are strings.
hints: Function to consider: isinstance(), inside a filter() lambda or list comprehension
isinstance(item, str) answers 'is this specifically a string' - it's the right tool here since type(item) == str would also work but isinstance() is the more idiomatic type check.
Return list(filter(lambda item: isinstance(item, str), items)), or the equivalent list comprehension.
expected_behavior: Returns only the string items, in their original order.
solution:
def get_string_lists(items):
    return [item for item in items if isinstance(item, str)]
explanation: isinstance() is the standard way to ask 'is this a string' in Python - it also correctly handles subclasses of str, which a strict type(item) == str comparison would not.
